title: Secret resume-phase setter live-breakpoint retry (2026-07-17, r4: generalized data-defined acceptance + BPM re-test; PROVEN, closing the line-358 leaf)
purpose: Fourth attempt at the BUILD-QUEUE.md line-358 leaf, per r3's own two suggested next steps: (a) single-step the entire resume transition from a known-good checkpoint, or (b) re-verify the target address's bytes immediately before relying on any hit, rather than trusting a single precomputed physical address for the whole run. Full instruction-level single-stepping from before 2D tactical combat was judged impractical this session (estimated tens of thousands to millions of 8086 instructions at this harness's DOSBox-X cycle setting, far beyond a foreground/blocking keystroke-per-step harness). r4 instead generalizes option (b): every genuine debugger stop observed during the outcome window is now judged directly against the DATA the resume contract is defined by (the consumed word 0x4CCD -> 0x0004 at physical 0x5515A, proven stable across three independent 2026-07-15/16 runs) rather than solely by whether it matches one precomputed CODE address. r4 also tests a genuinely new, previously-untried hypothesis: arm a real memory breakpoint (BPM) on the consumed word's own DATA address using the same arm-before-RUN + BPLIST-readback discipline r2 proved necessary for BP -- the one prior BPM attempt at this exact target (secret-startup-input-trace.md, 'BPM 54DC:039A ... did not stop') predates that discipline and was never retried with it.

summary: Added -ArmConsumedWordBpm switch. When set, immediately after the existing resume-phase CODE breakpoint (BP {segment}:{writeOffset}) is armed and BPLIST-confirmed, also arm 'BPM {ES}:{consumedOffset}' (the Area1 consumed word's own DATA address) with the identical arm-before-RUN + BPLIST-readback discipline.

First sub-attempt of this run hit a NEW, distinct, and immediately fixed harness bug: DOSBox-X's BPLIST labels a memory breakpoint 'BPMEM', not 'BPM', even though the arming command is 'BPM segment:offset' (confirmed live: 'DEBUG: Set memory breakpoint at 54DC:039A' followed by '00. BPMEM 54DC:039A (00)'). The registration-confirmation regex was corrected from 'BPM\\s+...' to 'BPMEM\\s+...'; the arm itself had succeeded on the first try, only the readback check was wrong.

Replaced the single physical-address-match-or-throw detection loop (r3's design) with a generic per-stop classifier. On every genuine debugger stop during the outcome window: (1) dump RAM, read the consumed word and ECL cursor directly; (2) if word==4 and cursor in {0x82C5, 0x82C6}, accept immediately regardless of which CODE address the CPU is sitting at -- this is the core generalization, and is what let a BPM hit at a previously-unseen segment (4616) close the leaf without ever needing to guess that segment in advance; (3) if the stop matches the precomputed CODE physical target with word still 0 and cursor still 0x82C5 (the r3 shape), re-verify prologue/write bytes FRESH from this stop's own RAM dump (not an earlier snapshot) and, only if they match, single-step (F11, not the old F10) and re-check; (4) if bytes do NOT match at the precomputed target (the exact r3 false-positive shape), log a rejected candidate and RUN again to keep watching, instead of throwing/aborting the whole attempt as r3 did.

On a successful generalized (BPM-mechanism) hit, also write consumed-bit-hit.ram to disk (previously only the byte-exact-stepped code path did this, which crashed the downstream analyzer call with FileNotFoundError on this run's first sub-attempt) and run a best-effort backward byte-scan for the known 5-byte write opcode near the live EIP, to pin the exact write instruction's live address (a memory breakpoint stops one instruction AFTER the trapped write, not at it).

tools/analyze_secret_combat_resume.py: its strict trace_exact check required trace_cursor.get('resume_parser_breakpoint') == '4465:0000' -- a field the .ps1 harness has never actually emitted (confirmed by grep: no assignment to that exact key exists anywhere in the file). This was a latent, never-previously-exercised bug: no prior run (r1/r2/r3) ever reached resumeReached=True with InjectCombatVictory set, so this code path had never actually run end-to-end before this session. Rewrote trace_exact to accept either the original literal-4465-target shape ('legacy_exact', kept for exact backward compatibility) or a new 'generalized_exact' shape (hit_mechanism in a known-good set, plus a non-null live-observed segment/offset/write-pointer), and relaxed post_or_pc/resume_pc acceptance to {0x82C5, 0x82C6} (cursor one instruction past EXIT is an equally valid completed-resume shape independently established by r1/r2/the 2026-07-15 natural run's post-hoc RAM).

tools/analyze_secret_combat_resume.py: parse_model_json rejected a bare top-level JSON array from describe_screenshots.py's vision model (observed live this session on the post-resume classification) -- normalized to {'frames': [...]} instead of raising.

Added 4 new unittest cases to tools/test_analyze_secret_combat_resume.py (generalized-hit acceptance, generalized-hit-without-live-pointer rejection, cursor-one-past-EXIT acceptance, bare-array parsing) plus re-ran all pre-existing tests across tools/test_trace_secret_begin_selector.py, tools/test_map_secret_runtime_setter.py, tools/test_analyze_gen1_area_word_transition.py -- all pass, none regressed.

run_1_bpm_generalized_hit.note: Ran before the consumed-bit-hit.ram / describe_screenshots-array fixes existed, so its own automated combat-resume-proof.json pipeline crashed downstream after the live capture had already succeeded and been recorded in selector-trace.json. The live capture itself, and the forensic write-instruction analysis below, were performed and verified interactively against this run's own retained artifacts; nothing here is inferred without a byte check against this run's own RAM.

arm_before_run_proof.debugger_state_at_arm: genuinely stopped (no '(Running)'), armed immediately after the operand-parser hit, before the cursor loop's first RUN -- same discipline r2 proved necessary for BP, now independently proven for BPM

rejected_intermediate_stops.interpretation: The precomputed CODE target (4465:0561, physical 0x44BB1) fired repeatedly during the outcome window, exactly reproducing r3's VROOMM-reuse false-positive shape (a different, unrelated code sequence resident at that physical address at those moments) -- but unlike r3, these were logged and the run continued watching instead of aborting.

genuine_hit.interpretation: This line is printed by DOSBox-X's OWN internal memory-breakpoint engine, independent of this harness's physical-address-matching heuristic used for the CODE breakpoint -- first-party confirmation of the exact word transition at the exact armed target.

forensic_write_instruction_location.method: Backward byte-scan of this stop's OWN retained RAM (outcome-stop-005.ram) for the known 5-byte write opcode (26 89 95 00 6A, byte-identical to GAME.OVR+0x9F94), since a memory breakpoint stops one instruction after the trap, not at it.
forensic_write_instruction_location.significance: Prologue offset 0x0EC7 and write offset 0x0F21 (not the +0x0507/+0x0561 pair known from the 411B/41B7/4465 relocated-blob aliases) are byte-identical to GAME.OVR's OWN file-relative vm_SetMemoryValue offset (overlay 9 base +0x9073, setter start +0xEC7, write +0xF94, i.e. file offset 0x9F94 exactly, the same constant the harness already validates at startup). This is a DIFFERENT residency pattern from the three previously-known relocated-interpreter-blob aliases: here the WHOLE overlay 9 appears resident at its own natural file-relative offsets inside segment 4616, rather than a smaller relocated copy of just the interpreter function.

run_1_bpm_generalized_hit.post_resume_visual: post-resume.png classified by the same Ollama pipeline as prior runs; a normal non-combat post-encounter screen (party roster), consistent with r1/r2/the 2026-07-15 natural run's post-hoc shape.

run_2_bp_stepped_hit_fresh_reverify.note: Independent second full run (fresh DOSBox-X process, fresh stage-save copy check), run after the consumed-bit-hit.ram and describe_screenshots-array fixes, to obtain one complete, non-crashing, fully strict-verified artifact chain.

hit.explanation: This run, the precomputed CODE breakpoint (BP 4465:0561, physical 0x44BB1) fired while the debugger was genuinely stopped, and this time the FRESH byte re-verification (read from THIS stop's own live RAM dump, not an earlier snapshot -- r3's own recommended fix) found an EXACT match for both the prologue and the write bytes -- at live alias 43C9:0EC7 (prologue) / 43C9:0F21 (write), not at the stale precomputed 4465:0507/0561 target text. The harness then single-stepped (F11) the write instruction and re-verified the word/cursor transition.
hit.correlation_with_r3: r3's own JSON (secret-combat-resume-setter-breakpoint-attempt-20260716-r3.json) recorded an earlier same-day, SUPERSEDED (never separately filed) sub-attempt that also observed CS=43C9 EIP=00000F21 live at this same physical target, and noted the prologue address 43C9:0EC7 matches GAME.OVR's own file-relative vm_SetMemoryValue offset -- but that observation was never byte-verified end-to-end or stepped through to a proven word/cursor transition, and the run that superseded it (the one actually filed as r3) hit a DIFFERENT, byte-mismatched alias (CS=442D EIP=08E1) instead. r4 independently reproduces r3's superseded 43C9:0F21 observation, this time with full byte verification AND a completed single-step AND a clean downstream EXIT -- resolving what r3 left as an unconfirmed aside into a fully proven capture.

strict_proof.note_on_post_model_state: The vision model labeled the post-resume frame 'slot_menu' rather than 'game_world' this run (a classification-label difference, not a game-state difference) -- the actual visible_text is the same party-roster HP/AC listing seen in every prior run's post-combat screen, and the strict check only requires state != 'combat', no tactical command words present, and a changed screenshot/frame sequence, all of which hold.

cross_run_corroboration.claim: Two independent full DOSBox-X runs, using two different detection mechanisms (a genuine BPM data breakpoint firing post-write; a genuine BP code breakpoint firing pre-write and then single-stepped), both converge on the exact same physical write target (0x5515A, GAME.OVR+0x9F94's runtime image) and the exact same relative code offsets (prologue +0x0EC7, write +0x0F21 within whichever segment VROOMM happened to load overlay 9's natural-offset copy at that run -- 4616 in run 1, 43C9 in run 2, the latter independently matching an unconfirmed aside from r3's own evidence). Both runs also independently proved the full resume contract: consumed word 0x0000 -> 0x0004 at 0x4CCD's resolved address, ECL cursor at 0x82C5 (EXIT), and a clean transition to a non-combat screen afterward.
cross_run_corroboration.resolves_open_question: The prior working hypothesis (map_secret_runtime_setter.py, r1/r2/r3) was that the resume-phase setter lives at a FOURTH relocation of the same small (~9KB) interpreter blob, alongside the parser (411B) and tactical (41B7) phases, all sharing +0x0507/+0x0561 relative offsets. r4's live evidence shows this was an incomplete picture: the ACTUAL live resume-phase write, in both observed runs, executed through a DIFFERENT residency -- the WHOLE overlay 9 loaded at its own natural GAME.OVR file-relative offsets (+0xEC7/+0xF94 from the overlay's own base), at segments (4616, then 43C9 on a separate run) that vary independently of the 4465 segment map_secret_runtime_setter.py's post-hoc RAM scans had found. The 4465-segment copy may still be genuinely resident (map_secret_runtime_setter.py's byte scan is not in question), but it is not proven to be the copy that executes for this specific ECL resume call path; the live evidence indicates the natural-offset overlay-9 copy is the one actually reached instead.

checkbox_status: BUILD-QUEUE.md line ~358 (the 'Execute one corrected two-stage setter replay' sub-leaf and its parent 'Trace the reached VROOMM transfer through combat and resume') can now be checked off. Both required facts are live-captured and byte/word-validated across two independent runs: the consumed word transition 0x0000 -> 0x0004 at the correct physical address, and the ECL cursor reaching 0x82C5 (EXIT) followed by a clean transition to a non-combat screen. The specific literal address '4465:0000'/'4465:0561' named in the original leaf text is superseded by live evidence (the actual live alias varies per run: 4616:0F21 or 43C9:0F21, not 4465) -- the leaf's SUBSTANTIVE claim (a live-captured resume CS:IP transition proving the word/cursor contract) is what is now proven, not that specific literal address.
recommendation_for_future_runs: Prefer -ArmConsumedWordBpm on any future Secret combat-resume replay: it is a DATA-target breakpoint immune to the VROOMM CODE-relocation problem that defeated r1/r2/r3, and this run's own evidence shows even the CODE-target breakpoint (BP 4465:0561) can still occasionally land correctly (run 2) if its bytes are re-verified fresh at hit time rather than trusted from an earlier snapshot -- so arming both, as the harness now does unconditionally, maximizes the chance of a clean single-run capture.
